about.title: Sebastopol Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Sebastopol's mix of small downtown storefronts, farm-to-market venues, and older apartment buildings means uneven walkways, wet floors, and poorly lit stairwells show up more often than people expect. Under California law, a property owner isn't automatically responsible just because someone got hurt on their premises — you generally need to show they knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and didn't fix it or warn visitors in time. That's why what happens in the minutes and days after a fall matters so much. Photos of the actual hazard, the names of any witnesses, and a written incident report can make the difference in a claim. Surveillance footage is often erased on a short cycle, so requesting it early is critical. If you were hurt in a fall anywhere in Sebastopol, from Bodega Avenue businesses to a residential complex off Petaluma Avenue, we can connect you with an attorney who reviews these details at no upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Your Fall

items.title: Notice Has to Be Proven
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An attorney can help gather maintenance logs, prior complaints, or repair records to establish this.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Claim
items.desc: Even if you're found partly at fault for not seeing a spill or a cracked step, California's pure comparative fault rule still lets you recover a share of damages tied to the property owner's responsibility.

items.title: Evidence Disappears Fast
items.desc: Surveillance video is often overwritten within days, and hazards get cleaned up quickly. An attorney can send preservation letters and gather evidence before it's gone.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Sebastopol?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a government entity, such as a public building or sidewalk maintained by the city, that deadline is much shorter and requires a separate claim process first. It's best to get guidance early so you don't lose the option to pursue a claim.

items.question: What if the store or landlord says it was my fault?
items.answer: That's a common response, but it doesn't end the conversation. California uses a pure comparative fault system, meaning you can still recover compensation even if you're partly responsible, though your share of fault can reduce the amount. An attorney can look at the specific facts, like lighting, signage, or how long the hazard existed, to evaluate the claim fairly.

items.question: I fell at a business near downtown Sebastopol — what should I do first?
items.answer: Try to photograph the exact spot and whatever caused the fall, whether it was a wet floor, a torn mat, or an uneven step, before it gets cleaned up or repaired. Ask an employee to document the incident and get names of anyone who saw it happen. Given Sebastopol's mix of small storefronts and older buildings, conditions can vary a lot from one property to the next, so specific documentation matters.
